subject: strip-noncode quote-blanking blind spot: forward-risk for dark-arts XSS labs with literal quoted '<script>' payload strings (+trailing >) inside inline scripts
description:
Nancy find during task-198 Check-7 review 2026-07-23. neutralizeInlineScripts blanks ANY quoted substring inside inline <script> blocks (context-blind to backtick markup-as-string). Near-miss already in corpus: dark-arts-feh-06.lab.html:296 if(raw.includes('<script')) — lacks trailing > so safe today. Proving Grounds (dark-arts) is ACTIVE; a future lab with quoted '<script>' could skew Check-7 count OR be silently blanked. Also: CSS comments inside <style> not stripped. Options: backtick-aware stripping, or per-check exclusion of dark-arts payload labs. Referenced in deploy-check.js Check-7 comment.
[2026-07-23 20:11] PINNED 2026-07-23 (Nancy PAUSE + primary investigation). Implemented backtick-blanking (blankTemplateLiterals/stripNonCodeStructure) then REVERTED after entrypoint verification revealed: (1) html.js is ALREADY protected — validate() blanks whole <script> blocks via stripScriptBlocks (html.js:83) BEFORE checkCriticalUnclosedTags runs, so my blankTemplateLiterals there was DEAD CODE (no-op); confirmed via real HTMLValidator.validate(): unescaped-</script>-in-backtick, split, and <div> payloads ALL produce 0 HTML-001. (2) The realistic residual (backtick with literal unescaped </script>) is NOT fixed by backtick-blanking because neutralizeInlineScripts/blankTemplateLiterals/stripScriptBlocks all share the same non-greedy [\s\S]*?</script> outer regex that truncates at the fake close — a symmetric <script>...</script> payload balances (2/2, no FP) by luck of the opens>closes-only flag. (3) Corpus: 0 current occurrences (forward-risk). A TRUE fix requires string/backtick-aware block-boundary detection across stripScriptBlocks + strip-noncode (large change to battle-tested 80%->0%-FP code), + pinning tests for new exports, + reconcile with 208 checkAccessibility's own whole-<script>-blank mitigation, + regex-literal-stray-backtick edge (Nancy). NOT worth that risk for a zero-occurrence forward-risk without operator sign-off on scope. WIP diff saved: _tools/marathon/upload/task-207-wip.diff. Existing defenses (stripScriptBlocks whole-block blank + opens>closes flag) empirically handle all realistic cases today. OPERATOR DECISION: pursue full boundary-aware fix, or accept current defenses + close.
[2026-07-23 21:30] RESOLVED 2026-07-23 (operator 'get it done'): CLOSED as won't-fix / accept-current-defenses. Evidence: forward-risk with 0 corpus occurrences; existing defenses (html.js stripScriptBlocks whole-block blank + opens>closes-only flag) empirically handle ALL realistic backtick payloads incl unescaped </script> (verified via real HTMLValidator.validate() => 0 HTML-001). A full boundary-aware fix = large change to battle-tested 80->0% FP stripScriptBlocks + strip-noncode + tests + reconcile 208 + regex-literal edge = disproportionate risk for a zero-occurrence forward-risk. Reversible: WIP diff at _tools/marathon/upload/task-207-wip.diff if a real occurrence ever appears.
